key: The thirty spokes unite in the one nave; but it is on the empty space (for the axle), that the use of the wheel depends.
s: Opening a chapter of three images, with vessel and room to follow, the verse gives the first; Wang Bi, on chapter 11, reads the nave as gathering its spokes through its non-being, which can receive things, and so holding the many together.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 11, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

opened.edition: zh.wikisource 道德經 (王弼本), the 華亭張氏 edition, revision 2354026
opened.locator: chapter 11, comment on 三十輻共一轂，當其無，有車之用

evidence.words: 轂所以能統三十輻者，無也，以其無能受物之故，故能以實統眾也。
evidence.gloss: What enables the nave to hold the thirty spokes together is non-being: because its non-being can receive things, it can, with its substance, unite the many.

reason: The amended rules hold against the old entry (54 words; its plain sense restated the key verse). Rewritten to 42 words: the plain sense now gives only context (the verse opens a chapter of three images, the wheel, then the clay vessel and the room, ending in a saying on existence and use) and repeats no run of the key verse. The reading keeps Wang Bi’s comment on exactly this line: the nave gathers (統) the thirty spokes by non-being (無), because non-being can receive things (無能受物), and so unites the many (統眾); 以實 is left out, so nothing beyond his words is claimed. Key, ref, at and src unchanged; verse.js ok (at [10]); entry-check ok.
